author: Nick Visser
description:
Friends and fans share memories of a man Donovan described as ‘a truly unique character’ and ‘a great Australian’

  • Molly Meldrum, Countdown host and promoter of Australian music, dies aged 83

  • Ian ‘Molly’ Meldrum – obituary

Friends and fans of Molly Meldrum have remembered the music industry great, who died Monday at the age of 83.

Meldrum spent more than a decade hosting ABC music show Countdown, leaving a lasting legacy on the Australian music landscape.

Continue reading...
title: Tributes flow for Molly Meldrum: Human Nature, Jason Donovan and more remember music industry great

author: Tom Lutz in New York and agencies
description:
• Ace’s contract reportedly for nine years

  • Mets have missed playoffs for last two seasons

The New York Mets look to have sealed the biggest deal of MLB’s offseason by signing free agent pitcher Tarik Skubal.

The New York Post’s Jon Heyman reported that the deal is worth $450m over nine years, the largest contract for a pitcher in baseball history. The previous record was for the $325m, 12-year deal Yoshinobu Yamamoto signed with the Dodgers in 2024.

Continue reading...
title: Mets reportedly agree $450m contract with Tarik Skubal, richest deal for pitcher in MLB history

author: Andy Hunter at Anfield
description:
• Manchester United lose 4-0 to Liverpool after early red

  • Argentinian suffers club’s joint-heaviest debut defeat

Mauricio Pochettino argued that Leny Yoro was wrongly sent off and that Manchester United were earlier denied a penalty against Liverpool after suffering the joint-heaviest debut defeat in the club’s history.

Liverpool’s emphatic 4-0 win ensured Pochettino equalled Lal Hilditch’s unwanted record from 1926 of losing his first United game by such a scoreline. United’s 34 goals conceded across all competitions this season are the most by any team in European football’s top five leagues.

Continue reading...
title: ‘It’s painful for me’: Pochettino criticises Yoro red card in Anfield humiliation

author: Agence France-Presse
description:
• Barça prevail 3-2 despite Lamine Yamal’s missed penalty

  • Juventus put four past Venezia, Paris FC climb to second

Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 at home on Sunday and restore their three-point lead at the top of La Liga.

Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou, and things got worse for Barça when winger Lamine Yamal missed a first-half penalty.

Continue reading...
title: European football: Barcelona roar back from two goals down to sink Villarreal

author: Reuters
description:
• Spaniard matches Giacomo Agostini’s premier-class tally

  • Márquez defends his title despite double surgery in May

Marc Márquez sealed the 2026 MotoGP world title at the Portuguese Grand Prix on Sunday, after his eighth-placed finish proved enough to establish an unassailable lead in the overall standings.

The Ducati rider needed to finish in the top nine in Sunday’s race and despite starting second on the grid, Márquez rode with caution to finish eighth and seal the title with a round to spare. The Spaniard’s eighth premier-class title puts him alongside the great Giacomo Agostini at the top of motorcycle racing’s all-time standings.

Continue reading...
title: Marc Márquez claims record-equalling eighth MotoGP world title in Portugal

author: Agencies
description:
• Incident occurred in Tampa on Friday morning

  • Crash leaves linebacker with serious injuries

Tampa police are investigating whether Tennessee Titans linebacker Jaylen Harrell assaulted a rideshare driver before a crash that left the NFL player in hospital.

The Tampa ⁠Police Department, in ⁠a preliminary report, said Harrell was in the back seat of the car around 8.45am on Friday in the backseat when “he reportedly assaulted the driver while ⁠the vehicle was in motion.” The driver then swerved, struck another car and collided ⁠with a utility pole, per the police report.

Continue reading...
title: NFL’s Jaylen Harrell reportedly assaulted driver before crash that left player seriously injured

author: Eric Berger
description:
The decline is costing colleges millions in tuition revenue and depriving American students of the cultural benefits of international classmates

Until 2025, students from Brazil, Nigeria, Thailand, Turkey, Turkmenistan and Zambia eagerly accepted a full scholarship to attend Indiana University in Bloomington, a town in the midwestern United States where fans are passionate about the Hoosiers – the school’s basketball and football teams.

The town also hosts the Little 500, a famous bicycle race that can attract more than 25,000 people. And most importantly for prospective students, the school has well-regarded academic programs.

Continue reading...
title: Trump’s immigration crackdown drives international students away from US universities

author: Giles Richards in Las Vegas
description:
• The Dutchman was under siege before pulling clear in the final lap

  • Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton once again clashed on the track

Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix with a remarkable, determined drive for Red Bull having done battle in a thrilling contest where the lead changed 35 times but the Dutchman remained absolutely indomitable, his skill and racecraft unmatched. His margin at the flag was just six-tenths of a second over the second -placed McLaren of Lando Norris, with his teammate Oscar Piastri finishing in third.

World Champion Kimi Antonelli who was in the fight was fourth and Alpine’s Pierre Gasly in fifth. George Russell, who vied for almost the entire race for the lead, was unlucky in running over debris at the death causing him to lock up and drop to ninth.

Continue reading...
title: Max Verstappen touches perfection in dramatic Las Vegas Grand Prix win

author: Pablo Iglesias Maurer at Audi Field
description:
• Current’s opener came direct from a corner kick

  • Debinha, Trinity Rodman trade goals in stoppage time

  • Washington Spirit lose third consecutive NWSL final

  • Read Jeff Rueter’s minute-by-minute report

It took five years, 90 minutes and a goal for the ages, but the Kansas City Current have their first-ever NWSL championship.

Riding a wave of momentum created by a 54th-minute Olimpico from midfielder Vanessa DiBernardo, and capping it off with an all-important breakaway winner from Debinha, the Current silenced the partisan, sellout crowd at the heavily-favored Washington Spirit’s home ground with a 2-1 victory on Saturday.

Continue reading...
title: Champion’s corner: KC Current win first NWSL Championship with 2-1 stunner over Spirit
